title: Dual conormal cokernel classifies square-zero algebra extensions
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow B=P/I$ be a surjective homomorphism of commutative $R$-algebras, with $n\geq0$ finite [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], and let $N$ be any $B$-module. Put $M=I/I^2$, $F=\bigoplus_{i=1}^n B\,\mathrm dx_i$, and $\delta:M\to F$, $[f]\mapsto\sum_i(\partial f/\partial x_i\bmod I)\mathrm dx_i$, the conormal differential [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Let $\operatorname{Exal}_R(B,N)$ be the isomorphism classes of exact sequences $0\to N\xrightarrow{j}E\xrightarrow{p}B\to0$ of additive groups in which $E$ is a commutative $R$-algebra, $p$ is an $R$-algebra map, $j(N)=\ker p$ has square zero, and multiplication induces the prescribed $B$-action on $N$. Isomorphisms induce the identity on $B$ and $N$. Equip these classes with Baer addition (fibre product over $B$, then pushout of the kernel along addition) and the $B$-action given by pushout along multiplication on $N$. There is a $B$-linear isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Exal}_R(B,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_B(M,N)/\{u\circ\delta:u\in\operatorname{Hom}_B(F,N)\}.$$
Under it the split extension $B\oplus N$, with multiplication $(b,n)(c,m)=(bc,bm+cn)$, corresponds to zero. For an extension and any lift $\widetilde\alpha:P\to E$ of the presentation map, its class corresponds to the class of $M\to N$, $[f]\mapsto j^{-1}(\widetilde\alpha(f))$. This isomorphism is natural in $N$: pushout along a $B$-linear map $v:N\to N'$ corresponds to postcomposition by $v$. No flatness, Noetherian or finite generation hypothesis on $I$ or $N$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0GPU, remark-extensions-of-algebras, lines 242-260: explicit cokernel and lifted-presentation formula; Baer addition and coefficient action are the corresponding fibre-product and pushout operations.

proof.text: Write $\alpha:P\twoheadrightarrow B$ for the presentation and $d_B:P\to F$ for $f\mapsto\sum_i\alpha(\partial_i f)\,\mathrm dx_i$. The polynomial differential basis and the universal property of differentials identify $R$-derivations $P\to N$ (with $P$ acting through $\alpha$) with $B$-linear maps $u:F\to N$, by $u\mapsto u d_B$. Indeed a $P$-linear map from the free differential module to $N$ is specified by the images of the $\mathrm dx_i$, and the same images specify a $B$-linear map from $F$. Leibniz gives $d_B(I^2)=0$ and $d_B(af)=\alpha(a)d_B(f)$ for $f\in I$, so restriction induces the stated $B$-linear $\delta:M\to F$. Thus $u\mapsto u\delta$ is $B$-linear, and its image is a submodule of $H=\operatorname{Hom}_B(M,N)$. Denote the quotient by $C_N$.

source.place: Tag 0GPU, conormal presentation and displayed cokernel; algebra.tex Tag 00RX, lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring

proof.text: Given an extension $E$, choose $e_i\in E$ above $\alpha(x_i)$. The polynomial universal property gives an $R$-algebra lift $a:P\to E$ with $a(x_i)=e_i$. Since $a(I)\subset j(N)$ and $j(N)^2=0$, restriction kills $I^2$. Define $\beta_a([f])=j^{-1}(a(f))$. It is additive; for $t\in P$ and $f\in I$, $a(tf)=a(t)j(\beta_a([f]))=j(\alpha(t)\beta_a([f]))$, proving $B$-linearity. Hence $[\beta_a]\in C_N$ is defined. An extension isomorphism carries a lift to a lift with exactly the same $\beta_a$.

source.place: Tag 0GPU, lifted presentation and its restriction to the ideal

proof.text: If $a,a'$ are two lifts, define $D(t)=j^{-1}(a'(t)-a(t))$. Expanding the product and using $j(N)^2=0$ gives $D(st)=\alpha(s)D(t)+\alpha(t)D(s)$; additivity and vanishing on $R$ follow by subtraction. Step 1 gives a unique $u:F\to N$ with $D=u d_B$, hence $\beta_{a'}-\beta_a=u\delta$. Conversely, for every $u$, $a'(t)=a(t)+j(u d_B(t))$ is an $R$-algebra lift: the same product expansion proves multiplicativity, and its unit and constants are unchanged. Its conormal map is $\beta_a+u\delta$. Consequently $c(E)=[\beta_a]$ is independent of the lift and defined on extension classes.

source.place: Tag 0GPU, independence of the lifted-presentation representative, expanded by the derivation calculation

proof.text: The quotient $A_0=P/I^2$ fits into the universal square-zero extension $0\to M\to A_0\to B\to0$: its kernel is $I/I^2$, its square is zero, and its action on that kernel factors through $B$. Given any $\beta\in H$, apply the coefficient-pushout lemma to this extension and $\beta:M\to N$. It gives an extension $E_\beta$ and a map $q_\beta:A_0\to E_\beta$ whose restriction to $M$ is $j_\beta\beta$. The composite $P\to A_0\to E_\beta$ is a lift with conormal map precisely $\beta$. Thus every element of $C_N$ occurs as $c(E_\beta)$.

source.place: Tag 0GPU, explicit conormal representative; Tag 0GPW, coefficient pushout construction

proof.text: For an arbitrary extension $E$ with lift $a$ and representative $\beta_a$, the lift kills $I^2$, so it descends to $\bar a:A_0\to E$. Its restriction to $M$ is $j\beta_a$. Apply the universal property of the pushout of $A_0$ along $\beta_a$, with target $E$ and $w=\operatorname{id}_N$. This gives $h:E_{\beta_a}\to E$ inducing the identity on $N$ and $B$. It is injective: $h(z)=0$ implies the image of $z$ in $B$ is zero, so $z=j_{\beta_a}(n)$ and $0=h(z)=j(n)$ forces $n=0$. It is surjective: for $e\in E$, choose $z$ above its image in $B$ and write $e-h(z)=j(n)$; then $h(z+j_{\beta_a}(n))=e$. Hence $h$ is an isomorphism of marked extensions.

source.place: Tag 0GPU, reconstruction from a lifted presentation; Tag 0GPW, universal property of coefficient pushout

proof.text: Suppose $c(E_1)=c(E_2)$. Choose lifts with representatives $\beta_1,\beta_2$. Equality in the quotient means $\beta_2-\beta_1=u\delta$ for some $u:F\to N$. Replace the lift in $E_1$ by $a_1+j_1u d_B$ as in Step 3; its representative is now $\beta_2$. Step 5 identifies both $E_1$ and $E_2$ with $E_{\beta_2}$ by isomorphisms fixing kernel and quotient. This proves injectivity, and Step 4 proves surjectivity. Thus $c$ is the asserted bijection with the prescribed representative formula.

source.place: Tag 0GPU, well-definedness and bijectivity of the explicit class map

proof.text: Let $v:N\to N'$ be $B$-linear. In the coefficient pushout $E_v$, the composite $q_va$ is a lift, and for $f\in I$ one has $(q_va)(f)=q_vj\beta_a([f])=j_vv\beta_a([f])$. Its representative is therefore $v\beta_a$. Postcomposition sends $u\delta$ to $(vu)\delta$, so this gives exactly the asserted map $C_N\to C_{N'}$ and proves naturality. For $b\in B$ take $v(n)=bn$: the class of the scalar pushout is $b[\beta_a]$.

source.place: Tag 0GPW, coefficient-pushout diagram and the paragraph identifying its class by Tag 0GPU

proof.text: For extensions $E_1,E_2$ with lifts $a_1,a_2$, their fibre product is the subring $E_1\times_BE_2=\{(e_1,e_2):p_1(e_1)=p_2(e_2)\}$ with componentwise operations. Projection to the common quotient is surjective, its kernel is $N\oplus N$, and this kernel is square zero with the componentwise $B$-action. The lift $t\mapsto(a_1(t),a_2(t))$ has representative $(\beta_1,\beta_2)$. Push out along $(n_1,n_2)\mapsto n_1+n_2$; the coefficient-pushout lemma and Step 7 give representative $\beta_1+\beta_2$. This is precisely Baer addition. For the split extension use $t\mapsto(\alpha(t),0)$; its representative is zero. Since $c$ is bijective and takes the specified addition and scalar operations to those of the quotient $B$-module, all module identities hold and $c$ is a $B$-linear isomorphism. These constructions only use finite polynomial lifts and square-zero multiplication, with no condition on $I$ or $N$.
